market_summary: US markets are selling off on post-midterm election uncertainty about data centre policy, hitting technology and AI stocks particularly hard. Nvidia tumbled 9.3% on November 5 amid concerns that Democratic election victories could lead to tighter restrictions on data centre construction. Tesla announced it will wind down Cybertruck production by mid-2027 after sales collapsed to roughly 10% of planned volumes. In Singapore, the three major banks reported Q3 results with mixed performance—OCBC beat expectations with record banking operations profit, while DBS and UOB disappointed, prompting multiple analyst target price cuts. Singapore Airlines confirmed further delays to its A350 cabin retrofit programme, now pushing new first and business class service to Q3/Q4 2027 due to supply chain constraints and seat certification issues.

items.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production by mid-2027
items.summary: Tesla will stop Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab production, after the vehicle sold at roughly 10% of planned 250,000 annual units, with only 20,237 sold in the U.S. in 2025.

items.headline: Nvidia tumbles 9.3% as AI stocks sell off on data centre policy concerns
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 9.26% to $181.60 on November 5 amid a broad AI chip selloff driven by post-midterm election concerns that Democratic control could tighten data centre construction regulations.

items.headline: OCBC posts 3% Q3 profit growth, beats expectations with record banking operations
items.summary: OCBC reported Q3 net profit of S$2.04 billion, up 3% year-on-year, with record banking operations profit of S$1.90 billion up 16%, and 9M26 net profit reaching record S$6.24 billion up 10%.

items.headline: Analysts cut DBS and UOB target prices after Q3 results miss on cautious 2027 guidance
items.summary: Multiple analysts cut DBS target prices by S$1-5 per share following lower earnings estimates, with Citi reducing to S$80.30 from S$86.60 and others following suit, as banks signal more cautious 2027 outlooks.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines delays A350 cabin retrofit to Q3/Q4 2027 due to certification issues
items.summary: SIA confirmed new first and business class products for A350 aircraft will not enter service until Q3/Q4 2027, delayed further from previous Q1 2027 target due to supply chain constraints and seat certification delays.

items.headline: Singtel executive Low Ka Hoe to become Netlink NBN Trust CEO
items.summary: Ex-ST Engineering and Singtel executive Low Ka Hoe will succeed Tong Yew Heng as CEO of Netlink NBN Trust, marking a leadership transition at the fibre infrastructure operator.
